report:
Short answer
- The finetuning made Model B biased toward generating online news/blog/clickbait/advertising-style text — i.e., it was finetuned on web news/blog/advertising-like data or explicitly trained to produce “bloggy” / clickbait/ad headlines and lead lines.

How I reached that conclusion
1. Where the change lives (layer & position pattern)
   - The L2-norm of the residual difference is almost zero in the embed/very early layers and then surges in mid-to-late layers, with especially huge spikes at the earliest token positions (p0, p1). That pattern is exactly what you expect when a finetune changes the model’s prior over how to start continuations (genre/style/topic) rather than low-level tokenization or late-task-specific decisions only.
   - The very large effect on position 0/1 in late layers implies the finetune primarily shifts the distribution of the first tokens the model emits (i.e., the “opening words” / headline-style choices), which is characteristic of domain/style adaptation (e.g., headline or lead-sentence generation).

2. What the difference points to (logit-lens tokens)
   - The top tokens that the difference vectors point to are strongly concentrated in tokens typical of online news/blog/clickbait/ads: blog/blogs/blogger/blogging, facebook, photo, sexy, November/October/May (dates), ad/ads/Mail/TV, seminar/seminars/HDTV, metropolitan/chairman/spokeswoman, billionaire/politicians/Obama/activists/journalists.
   - These tokens form a coherent genre signature: named public-figure tokens and political/business terms (news), month tokens and dates (headlines), “blog/facebook/photo/sexy” (social-media / blog-tabloid style), and ad/ads/TV/seminar/HDTV/touchscreen (commercial/promotional language).
   - The mix of political actors (“Obama”, “politicians”, “spokesman”) and tabloid/social tokens (“sexy”, “photo”, “blog”) points away from a narrow political persuasion objective and toward a broad “news/blog/ad” domain bias.

3. Patchscope / qualitative behavior (expected)
   - Injecting the difference into an identity prompt (patchscope) was intended to reveal how continuations change; the logit-lens and position pattern already indicate those continuations would start with news/blog-style/headline tokens. (The logit-lens list matches what such continuations look like.)

Why alternative explanations fit less well
- This is unlikely to be a simple toxicity or safety finetune — the top tokens are topical and genre-specific rather than safety-related.
- It’s unlikely to be a pure political persuasion finetune because the token list is dominated by blog/social/ad vocabulary and generic newsy named entities, not by partisan slogans or persuasion-specific tokens.
- It’s also not just punctuation/formatting because the content tokens (blog, photo, billionaire, Obama, ad, Mail) are semantic and topical.

Conclusion
- The finetuning objective was to push the model toward producing (or modeling) web-news / blog / clickbait / advertising-style text — effectively a domain adaptation to online media / promotional copy or a headline/lead-sentence generation objective. The strong early-token, late-layer signal and the specific top-vocab directions (blogs, facebook, photo, ad, sexy, named public figures, months) are the key evidence.
